meta.title: Decision-blocking questions register
meta.purpose: Every question that must be answered before a decision can be made, split into what we already know, what we do not know, and what specific evidence would close the gap.
meta.how_to_use: Answer a question by writing the answer and its source into 'answer' and flipping status to 'answered'. Nothing here is answered by assumption.

questions.question: What home-field advantage should the line model use?
we_know: nfl.com publishes home and road win-loss records for all 32 teams (S01).
The repo has 32 teams and 274 team-games of PF/PA.
we_do_not_know: Home and road points scored/allowed by team.
Any league-wide estimate of HFA for 2026.
evidence_needed: A source publishing home/away point splits (nfl.com standings does not).
Or compute it once per-team game logs are available.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Every modelled line stays compressed toward pick'em and is not comparable to a market line.

questions.question: Where does settled-bet history come from, and who grades it?
we_know: No settled bets exist in the repo.
we_do_not_know: Whether a historical closing-line source is obtainable.
How results will be graded and by whom.
evidence_needed: A settled-bet ledger with price taken, closing price and result per bet.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The leaderboard remains empty and no strategy can pass gate G1.

questions.question: Which official injury snapshot is the reference for grading - Friday's report, or the 90-minute inactives list?
we_know: nfl.com publishes game status (Out/Doubtful/Questionable) on the injury report (S02).
A separate inactives list is published closer to kickoff.
we_do_not_know: The inactives list for Week 10 was not captured.
evidence_needed: The Week 10 inactives list at kickoff, captured and stored.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Injury signals cannot be graded correctly: a Questionable player who sits is currently indistinguishable from one who plays.

questions.question: Can a licensed, timestamped closing-line source be obtained?
we_know: No odds feed is reachable from this environment; no odds data is in the repo.
we_do_not_know: Whether the user has an account or licence that could supply it.
evidence_needed: A data agreement or API key for a licensed odds provider, plus storage in the repo's external-storage convention.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Gate G4 cannot be evaluated and the site cannot show whether a model line beat the market.

questions.question: How should disagreements between Ourlads and the official NFL report be governed?
we_know: 14 disagreements were found in Week 10 alone (data/depth_risk.json -> conflicts).
The official report is the league's own publication.
we_do_not_know: Whether the NFL publishes a machine-readable depth chart at all.
evidence_needed: Confirm whether an official depth-chart feed exists.
questions.answer: Proposed and implemented: the official NFL report governs availability; Ourlads governs depth ORDER only. Every disagreement is published. A reviewer should confirm or overrule this.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Without a rule the two sources silently contradict each other 14 times a week.

questions.question: Which player-level stat source will be the baseline for prop modelling?
we_know: A league-wide player-statistics endpoint was confirmed reachable and returns real 2026 data (ESPN byathlete API), but it was not ingested.
we_do_not_know: Whether it is complete enough to grade props.
Its terms of use for republication.
evidence_needed: A deliberate ingest decision plus a licence check before publishing derived numbers.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: No prop or prop-combo strategy can move past 'blocked-input'.

questions.question: Which correlations are real, and at what value?
we_know: The engine prices two-leg parlays with a Gaussian copula and refuses to price when rho is unset.
At rho=0.6, two 55% legs move from 30.25% (naive) to 40.35% (copula).
we_do_not_know: Any empirical rho - none has been estimated from data in this repo.
evidence_needed: Per-player game logs to estimate rho for each proposed pair.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Parlays stay unpriced rather than mispriced.

questions.question: What is the pre-registered rule for calling a strategy 'skill based'?
we_know: Six procedures (L1-L6) are specified in data/strategies.json.
we_do_not_know: The pass threshold for each, and who signs off.
evidence_needed: Agreed thresholds before any results are seen - pre-registration is the point.
questions.answer: Proposed: all of L1, L4 and L5 must pass, plus a positive bootstrap 5th percentile. A reviewer should ratify or change this BEFORE results exist.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Thresholds chosen after seeing results are not evidence.

questions.question: What does the leaderboard reward, and who funds it?
we_know: A three-tier design and a risk-adjusted, deflation-corrected scoring rule are proposed in data/strategies.json.
we_do_not_know: The reward medium, budget and governance.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The competition exists on paper only and allocates nothing.

questions.question: How often must the injury and depth data be refreshed, and by what process?
we_know: The capture in this repo is a snapshot from 2026-11-14 and will be stale the moment Week 11 reports publish.
we_do_not_know: Whether an automated refresh is possible in this environment (external fetch is tool-mediated, not scriptable with curl).
evidence_needed: An agreed refresh cadence and an execution path.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Pages will silently age. Every page carries its as-of date and a staleness banner.

questions.question: 27 of 32 depth charts are transcribed. Does full league coverage change any conclusion?
we_know: Indianapolis is missing; the four bye teams (CHI, DEN, PHI, TB) do not play this week.
we_do_not_know: Whether the missing chart would move a team into the top of the index.
evidence_needed: Fetch and transcribe the Colts chart (flagged F-06).
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The ranking is correct for 27 teams and silent on one.

questions.question: Is draft pedigree an acceptable proxy for replacement quality?
we_know: Pedigree is published and verifiable (S04 draft codes, S05 key).
It is a proxy, not a measurement - a 7th-rounder who has played well scores badly.
we_do_not_know: Snap counts, PFF-style grades, or any per-player performance measure - none are in the repo.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The exposure ranking is directionally defensible but not precise, and is labelled that way.

questions.question: What does publishing model lines imply in the user's jurisdiction?
we_know: The user is in Mexico City; the site is public on GitHub Pages.
we_do_not_know: Whether line publication triggers any licensing or gambling-advice obligation.
questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The site carries a no-betting-advice disclaimer and publishes no odds.
